important.name: check_links crashes on a malformed href
important.reviewer: runtime, docs, skill_package, overall, system_shape, tests
important.summary:
_is_relative (line 75) and _link_problem (line 82) call urlsplit(href) unguarded. urlsplit raises a plain ValueError on a malformed authority such as href="http://[" (Invalid IPv6 URL). Nothing catches it, so one bad href in a tool's canonical XML aborts check_links for the whole tool instead of reporting a problem. HelpError subclasses ValueError, but callers that catch HelpError do not catch the bare ValueError, and the module docstring promises one problem per bad href. No test feeds a malformed href.

Also (runtime): urlsplit reads a drive letter as a scheme: href="C:\x.html" or "C:/x.html" gets scheme 'c'. _is_relative returns False for it and _link_problem returns None because the scheme is not 'file'. A local path that is dead on every other machine is therefore treated like a web link and goes unreported. An href rooted at '/' or '\' (including a UNC path '\\server\share\x.html') is also excluded from link_relative by _is_relative, and then returns None because its scheme is empty, so it gets no code at all. The _link_problem docstring (line 79) says None is only for an anchor, a non-file: link or a present target, and the module docstring (lines 8-12) does not say what happens to rooted paths. The code contradicts both. No test covers either case.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:124 promises one problem per defective href, but `_is_relative` (arc_help_pages_api.py:75) and `_link_problem` (line 82) call `urlsplit(href)` unguarded. An href such as `http://[` raises `ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL` (confirmed on the project interpreter), so `check_links` stops at the first such href. harness-skill-api turns this into `problem: ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL`, which names neither the tool nor the href, and every later href in the XML goes unchecked. No plan test covers a malformed href.

Also (docs): SKILL.md:124 says only `#` anchors and web links are skipped, but the code skips more. `urlsplit(r'C:\x.html').scheme` is `c`, so a Windows path counts as a non-`file:` link and is skipped like a web URL (api.py:82). An href starting with `/` or `\` is excluded from `link_relative` (api.py:75) and also has no `file` scheme, so it gets no code either. Both are dead on Pro's temp copy and in production, like an outside `file:` href, yet `check_links` prints `clean`. The module docstring (api.py:8-12) says other schemes are skipped and rooted hrefs are not relative, which matches the code, but neither it nor SKILL.md says that such hrefs are never reported. arc-meta's SKILL.md lists the allowed absolute forms as a `file:///` URI, a web URL or a `#` fragment, and neither of these is one.

Also (skill_package): _is_relative (line 75) and _link_problem (line 82) call urllib.parse.urlsplit on every href without catching ValueError. An href such as http://[ makes urlsplit raise 'Invalid IPv6 URL', so check_links aborts on that href: no problem for it and none for any later href. Through harness-skill-api the whole call becomes one bare 'problem: Invalid IPv6 URL' line that names neither the tool nor the href; called as a library it escapes as a raw ValueError, not a HelpError. The SKILL.md contract (line 124, one problem per defective href) and the API docstring (lines 8-12) do not allow either result. The plan's tests do not cover this.

Also (skill_package): _link_problem reports only file: hrefs and hrefs with no scheme that are not rooted. urlsplit reads a Windows drive path such as C:\x.html or E:/other/x.html as scheme 'c' or 'e', so line 82 treats it as a web link and returns None. An href that starts with / or \ fails _is_relative (line 75) and then has no file scheme, so it also returns None. Both kinds are local file references that break when Pro renders the '?' page from its temp copy. arc-meta's SKILL.md allows only a file:/// URI, a web URL or a # fragment. So check_links prints 'clean' for exactly the links its Judgment table tells the agent to replace. SKILL.md line 124 lists only '#' anchors and web links as skipped, so the root-relative case also contradicts the documented contract. The plan's tests do not cover either kind.

Also (overall): _is_relative (line 75) and _link_problem (line 82) call urllib.parse.urlsplit on every href without a guard. urlsplit raises a bare ValueError ('Invalid IPv6 URL') for an href such as http://[ or https://[::1, so check_links aborts on the first such href: no problem list comes back, every other href's report is lost, and harness-skill-api prints a generic 'problem: ... Invalid IPv6 URL' line with no code and no href. The docstring (lines 8-12) and the SKILL.md API table promise one problem per defective href. No test feeds a malformed href.

Also (overall): _link_problem skips every href whose scheme is not 'file'. A Windows path such as C:\x.html or C:/x.html parses with scheme 'c', so it is skipped as a web link although it names a local file that is dead in production (the case link_outside_checkout exists for). An href rooted at / or \ (/x.html, \x.html, //host/x.html) is excluded from link_relative by _is_relative (line 75) and then has scheme '' != 'file', so it falls through to None at line 83 and gets no code at all, though it resolves against the drive of Pro's temp copy. check_links therefore reports 'clean' for links that are broken in Pro. The docstring (lines 8-12) and the SKILL.md check_links row describe the skip of 'schemes other than file:' as covering web links only; neither case is tested.

Also (system_shape): `_is_relative` (line 75) and `_link_problem` (line 82) call `urlsplit(href)` without a guard. An href such as `http://[` makes `urlsplit` raise `ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL`, which is neither caught in `check_links` nor a `HelpError`. The whole check stops and `harness-skill-api` prints one `problem: ValueError: Invalid IPv6 URL` line. That line names neither the tool nor the href, and every other href in the file goes unchecked. This contradicts SKILL.md:124 (`check_links` returns 'one problem per defective href') and the module docstring (lines 8-12), which promise a per-href report. No test covers a malformed href.

Also (system_shape): `urlsplit('C:\\x.html').scheme` is `c`, so `_link_problem` (line 82) treats a Windows path as a non-`file:` link and returns None. An href starting with `/` or `\\` is excluded from `link_relative` by `_is_relative` (line 75), then also returns None at line 82 because its scheme is not `file`. Neither kind gets a code. Both are dead in production and resolve against the drive of Pro's temp copy, which is the same reason `link_outside_checkout` and `link_relative` exist. SKILL.md:124 says only '`#` anchors and web links are skipped', and the plugin README:32-34 says `check_links` reports every href whose target is missing, outside the checkout or relative. The code skips two kinds that are not web links, so the docs and the behavior disagree and a broken link reports `clean`.

Also (runtime): _link_problem strips '#...'/'?...' and unquotes the tail before resolving it, so 'file:///<checkout>/<help_dir>/page.html#parameters' counts as a valid link. _links_page compares the raw href tail to the page path exactly, so the same href is reported as help_page_unlinked, and so is an href whose path is percent-encoded (spaces as %20). The two checks disagree about what counts as a link to the page.

Also (skill_package): _link_problem accepts any href whose start matches the main-checkout prefix, then checks (p.root / tail).is_file(). An href such as <prefix>../other-repo/x.html passes the prefix test and resolves outside the checkout. If that file exists, check_links reports nothing, although the API docstring (lines 9-11) says an href outside the checkout is link_outside_checkout.

Also (overall): _link_problem accepts any href under the prefix and tests (p.root / tail).is_file(). A tail such as ../other-repo/x.html (or tool_metadata/../../x.html) names a file outside the checkout; when that file exists the href is reported clean, though it is not a page of this repository and is dead in production.

Also (tests): _is_relative (arc_help_pages_api.py:75) and _link_problem (:82) call urlsplit on every href without a guard. urlsplit raises ValueError('Invalid IPv6 URL') for an href such as http://[ or file://[, so check_links (and through _hrefs nothing else) ends in a traceback instead of a problem line. HelpError subclasses ValueError, but the ValueError from urlsplit carries no HelpError type and no caller catches it. The check exists to report bad hrefs in hand-written canonical XML, so a malformed one is exactly the input it must survive. The link tests (test_check_links_* at lines 117-168) feed only well-formed hrefs, so the crash is uncovered.

Also (tests): An href like C:\x.html parses with scheme 'c', so _is_relative is False and _link_problem returns None at arc_help_pages_api.py:82-83 as if it were a web link. An href rooted at / or \ (including a UNC \\server\share path) is excluded from link_relative by the startswith check at :75 and then also returns None at :82, since its scheme is empty, not 'file'. Both kinds are dead or machine-specific in the rendered help page, the same defect class link_outside_checkout and link_relative report, yet nothing reports them. test_check_links_ignores_anchors_and_web_links (lines 136-139) and test_check_links_reports_relative_hrefs (142-149) never feed either form, so the gap is not pinned in either direction.

Also (tests): test_check_links_matches_the_prefix_ignoring_case[lower_drive] relies on _lower_drive (lines 152-154), which only changes a prefix holding a drive letter. On Ubuntu the prefix is file:///tmp/..., so the case runs the unchanged prefix and cannot fail for the drive-case reason it names; the test carries no cross_os marker, so the Windows CI job, the only place a drive letter exists, never runs it.
fix: Add a helper `_scheme(href) -> Optional[str]` that wraps urlsplit in try/except ValueError and returns None on failure. When it returns None, _link_problem reports a new HelpProblemCode.LINK_MALFORMED ('link_malformed', detail = href) and _is_relative uses the helper too. Add the code to the HelpProblemCode enum, the module docstring and the skill's problem list, plus a test with href="http://[".
Catch ValueError in _link_problem and report the href under an existing code (link_relative, with a detail that says it is malformed), plus a test with href="http://[".

Before the scheme test in _link_problem, treat a single-letter scheme (or a match of `^[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`) and a rooted href that does not start with '//' as a local path outside the checkout: report link_outside_checkout. Update the module docstring (lines 8-12) and the _link_problem docstring, and add tests for 'C:\x.html', 'C:/x.html', '/x.html' and '\\server\x.html'.
Add a dedicated HelpProblemCode (for example 'link_local_path') for drive-letter, rooted and UNC hrefs, documented in the module docstring, with the same tests.

Parse each href once in `_link_problem` inside `try: parts = urlsplit(href) except ValueError:` and return a problem for that href (a new `link_malformed` code in `HelpProblemCode`, documented in the SKILL.md:124 API row and the module docstring, or `link_relative` with a `malformed:` detail), then add a `test_check_links_reports_a_malformed_href` case to tests/arc/test_arc_help_pages_api.py

In `_link_problem`, treat a one-letter scheme (a drive path) and an href rooted at `/` or `\` as `link_outside_checkout`, or as a new code. Skip only real web schemes (`http`, `https`, plus `mailto` if wanted) instead of every non-`file` scheme. Add test cases for `C:\x.html`, `/x.html` and `\\server\x.html`, and update the SKILL.md:124 row and the api.py module docstring to list exactly what is skipped
If skipping them is intended, say so in SKILL.md:124 and the arc-straps README Check bullet: 'drive paths, rooted paths and every non-file: scheme are not checked'

Parse each href once in a helper that catches ValueError from urlsplit and returns a problem for that href, e.g. a new HelpProblemCode.LINK_MALFORMED ('link_malformed', subject tool, detail the href). Then check_links goes on to the remaining hrefs. Add the code to arc_help_pages_models.HelpProblemCode, the check_links row of SKILL.md and the API docstring, and add a test with http://[ followed by a valid href.
Alternatively report a malformed href as link_relative or link_outside_checkout, with the parse error in the detail, and document that in SKILL.md line 124.

Treat a one-letter scheme (a drive letter) and an href rooted at / or \ as local paths: report them as link_outside_checkout, or as a new code such as link_not_uri. Skip only real web schemes (http, https, mailto, ...) and '#' anchors. Update the check_links row of SKILL.md and the API docstring, and add tests for C:\x.html and /x.html.
At minimum, list these hrefs as skipped in SKILL.md line 124 and the API docstring lines 8-12, and add a Judgment row telling the agent to replace them with the development href.

Route both urlsplit calls through one helper, e.g. _scheme(href) -> Optional[str], that catches ValueError and returns None; report a None scheme as a problem naming the href (a new HelpProblemCode such as link_malformed, added to arc_help_pages_models.py, test_problem_codes_spell_the_spec_values, the module docstring and the SKILL.md check_links row), and add a test_check_links case with href="http://[" asserting the problem and that a valid href next to it is still checked.
At minimum, catch the ValueError in _link_problem and re-raise HelpError naming the href and the tool, so the refusal says which link to fix; add the same test asserting HelpError.

Classify before the scheme test: an href matching ^[A-Za-z]:[\\/] is a local path (convert with Path(href).as_uri() and run the prefix check, or report link_outside_checkout directly); an href starting with / or \ (including //host) with no scheme is reported (link_relative, or link_outside_checkout, with the detail naming it). Skip only '#' anchors and an explicit allow-list of web schemes (http, https, mailto). Update the module docstring, the SKILL.md check_links row and add test_check_links cases for C:\x.html, C:/x.html, /x.html and \x.html.

Add a helper `_scheme(href) -> Optional[str]` that wraps `urlsplit(href).scheme` in `try/except ValueError` and returns None for a malformed href. Use it in `_is_relative` and `_link_problem`, and report the malformed href as its own problem with the href as detail: either a new `HelpProblemCode.LINK_MALFORMED` (update models, `test_problem_codes_spell_the_spec_values`, the SKILL.md API table and the Judgment table), or `link_relative` if a new code is not wanted. Add a `test_check_links_reports_a_malformed_href` case using `http://[` beside a valid href, asserting that both hrefs are evaluated.

In `_link_problem`, skip only anchors and an explicit allow-list of web schemes (`http`, `https`, `mailto`). Report a one-letter scheme (a drive path) and a root-anchored href (`/...`, `\\...`) as `link_outside_checkout`, since neither names the main checkout's `file:` prefix. Update the module docstring (lines 8-12) and SKILL.md:124 to list exactly what is skipped, and add parametrized cases for `C:\\x.html`, `/x.html` and `\\\\server\\x.html` to `tests/arc/test_arc_help_pages_api.py`.

If rooted paths are meant to stay unchecked, say so in SKILL.md:124 and in the module docstring (`rooted paths and any non-file: scheme are skipped`), and still report a drive-letter scheme as `link_outside_checkout`.

Factor the tail normalization out of _link_problem (split on [#?], then unquote) into a helper and use it in both functions. _links_page then compares the normalized tail to the repo-relative page path. Add a test with a '#parameters' suffix.
Resolve the target and require (p.root / tail).resolve().is_relative_to(p.root.resolve()). Report link_outside_checkout when it is not, and add a test for an href that uses '..'.

Resolve the target and require it under the root: target = (p.root / tail).resolve(); report link_outside_checkout when not target.is_relative_to(p.root.resolve()), else check is_file(); add a test with prefix + '../x.html' pointing at an existing file outside the project.

Parse each href once in _link_problem inside try/except ValueError and return a problem for it (an existing code such as link_outside_checkout with the parser message in the detail, or a new link_malformed code added to HelpProblemCode and to test_problem_codes_spell_the_spec_values); then add a test in tests/arc/test_arc_help_pages_api.py that links 'http://[' through _usage and asserts check_links returns that code instead of raising.

In _link_problem, treat an href matching ^[A-Za-z]:[\\/] and an href starting with / or \ as a local path: report it as link_outside_checkout (or a new code) with the href as detail; add parametrized cases 'C:\\x.html', '/x.html' and '\\\\srv\\x.html' to test_arc_help_pages_api.py asserting that code, and update the api module docstring that says rooted hrefs are not relative.
Add @pytest.mark.cross_os to test_check_links_matches_the_prefix_ignoring_case (line 157) so the Windows job exercises the drive-letter case.

important.name: Fragment sections may reuse an id, including the generated parameters and syntax ids
important.reviewer: runtime, docs, skill_package, overall, system_shape, tests
important.summary:
_check_sections refuses only a <section> with no id or no <h2>. A fragment section with id="parameters" or id="syntax" is accepted, and so are two fragment sections that share an id. render() then emits a page with two elements carrying the same id. _nav lists both sections with the same '#id' anchor, so one nav link jumps to the wrong section. The fragment contract in the module docstring (lines 3-6) is meant to make the page well-formed, and the generated sections _parameters_section (line 147) and _syntax_section (line 158) hard-code those two ids.

Also (docs): The build generates `<section id="parameters">` and `<section id="syntax">` (arc_help_pages_build.py:147,158). `_check_sections` (build.py:88-94) only refuses a section without an id or an `<h2>`, so a fragment section with `id="parameters"` or `id="syntax"`, or two fragment sections with the same id, gets through. The built page then has duplicate ids, and `_nav` (build.py:171-173) emits two links to the same anchor, which both land on the first section. SKILL.md:31-34 does not say these ids are reserved.

Also (skill_package): _check_sections refuses a <section> only when it has no id or no <h2>. A fragment section with id="parameters" or id="syntax" passes. _parameters_section and _syntax_section (lines 147, 158) then emit sections with those same ids, so the built page holds two elements with one id. The nav (_nav, line 171) lists both entries with the same #anchor, and the browser jumps to the first, which may be the wrong section. Two fragment sections that share any id fail the same way. check_help_page still reports the page clean. SKILL.md line 32 promises each section 'with an id', and the build docstring line 6 says the nav lists each section in page order, but neither works with duplicate ids. The plan's tests do not cover this.

Also (overall): _check_sections refuses a <section> without an id or an <h2> but never compares ids. A fragment section with id="parameters" or id="syntax" is accepted, and the built page then holds two sections with that id (the generated ones carry those ids, lines 147 and 158): the nav lists the id twice and both links jump to the first. Two hand-written sections sharing an id slip through the same way. The page is accepted, written by apply_help and reported current by check_help_page. REFUSALS in test_arc_help_pages_build.py has no duplicate-id case.

Also (system_shape): `_check_sections` (lines 88-94) refuses a `<section>` without an `id` or an `<h2>`, but it never checks that ids are unique or that the fragment avoids `parameters` and `syntax`. The generated sections always use those two ids (`_parameters_section` line 147, `_syntax_section` line 158). A fragment section with `id="parameters"`, or two fragment sections sharing an id, builds without complaint. The page then holds duplicate ids, and the nav (`_nav`, lines 171-173) lists two entries that jump to the same first element, so the generated Parameters or syntax section cannot be reached from the nav. SKILL.md:32 and SKILL.md:41 describe the nav as listing each section by its id, which holds only when ids are unique. No refusal case in `test_fragment_refusals` covers it.

Also (tests): _check_sections (arc_help_pages_build.py:88-94) refuses a section without an id or an h2 but never checks the id against the generated sections' ids or against each other. A fragment holding <section id="parameters"> (or id="syntax", or two sections with one id) builds a page with duplicate ids, so the nav anchor lands on whichever comes first and the page is invalid HTML. The REFUSALS table in test_arc_help_pages_build.py (lines 106-113) lists no_section_id and no_section_h2 only, so this refusal is neither implemented nor tested.
fix: In _check_sections, track the ids already seen, seeded with the reserved {'parameters', 'syntax'}. Raise FragmentError(f"fragment {page}: <section id=\"{section_id}\"> repeats an id") (naming the reserved ids when that is the clash). Mention the rule in the module and parse_fragment docstrings and add tests for id="parameters", id="syntax" and a duplicated custom id.

In `_check_sections`, raise `FragmentError(f"fragment {page}: <section id=\"{id}\"> repeats an id")` for a repeated id, and refuse `parameters` and `syntax` as reserved for the generated sections. Name the reserved ids in SKILL.md:31-34, and add a build test for each case

In _check_sections, collect the ids and raise FragmentError for an id of 'parameters' or 'syntax' (the ids the generated sections own), and for any id seen twice. Name both in the SKILL.md fragment bullet (line 32) and the parse_fragment docstring, and add tests for a reserved id and for a duplicate id.

In _check_sections, collect the ids in order and raise FragmentError for an id in {"parameters", "syntax"} (name it as reserved for the generated section) and for any id seen twice; add REFUSALS cases 'reserved_parameters_id', 'reserved_syntax_id' and 'duplicate_id' using the extra= argument of fragment(), and state the rule in the SKILL.md fragment bullet (line 32) and the module docstring (lines 3-6).

In `_check_sections`, collect the ids and raise `FragmentError` for an id in `{"parameters", "syntax"}` (name it as reserved for a generated section) and for any id seen twice. Add `reserved_parameters_id`, `reserved_syntax_id` and `duplicate_id` entries to `REFUSALS` in `tests/arc/test_arc_help_pages_build.py`, and state in SKILL.md:31-34 that section ids are unique and that `parameters` and `syntax` are reserved.

minor.name: arc-straps README describes help_dir and Requirements as single-skill
minor.summary:
The `help_dir` row (README.md:126) describes the folder as holding the help pages `<Tool>.html`. The pages are actually `<page>.html`, named after the fragment stem (SKILL.md:11-12, api.py:137), and the folder also holds `_template.html`, `_fragments/` and `img/` (SKILL.md:26-37). Requirements (README.md:48) says only that nothing in `arc-meta` imports arcpy, though the plugin now has two skills and neither imports it.

Also (skill_package): The arc_help_pages config table describes help_dir as 'Folder of the tracked help pages, <Tool>.html', and the schema description repeats it. The skill names pages by the fragment stem <page> ('usually the tool name', SKILL.md lines 11-12, 35), and its own README Build bullet (line 29) says <help_dir>/<page>.html. The table also leaves out the _fragments/ folder and _template.html, which the schema description mentions.

Also (system_shape): The schema description (`arc-straps.schema.json` `help_dir`) and the plugin README key table (README.md:126) describe `help_dir` as the folder of `<Tool>.html`. The build writes `<help_dir>/<page>.html`, where `<page>` is the fragment stem (`apply_help` line 226). SKILL.md:11-12 says the page name is 'usually the tool name', and the tool comes from the fragment's tool line. The docs name the wrong key for the file name.

Also (system_shape): README.md:48-50 says 'Nothing in `arc-meta` imports arcpy; it needs the standard library and pydantic', although the PR adds a second skill with the same requirement. A reader cannot tell whether `arc-help-pages` needs ArcGIS Pro.
fix: README.md:126: `Folder of the help pages, `<page>.html`, with `_template.html`, `_fragments/` and `img/``. README.md:48: `Nothing in `arc-meta` or `arc-help-pages` imports arcpy`

minor.name: arc_help_pages schema descriptions hide that the section does not follow arc_meta
minor.summary: The arc_help_pages.atbx and arc_help_pages.tool_dir descriptions are copied word for word from arc_meta, so a project that overrides arc_meta.atbx or arc_meta.tool_dir (README example: "atbx": "MyTools.atbx") sees nothing in the schema hint telling it the same values must also be set here. arc_help_pages_config.paths() resolves this section on its own (its own defaults, its own _only_archive lookup). If the project root holds two archives, help pages raise a ConfigError; if it uses another XML folder, they silently read the default tool_metadata/tools. README.md lines 116-118 say the section 'resolves apart from arc_meta', but the schema description is the text an editor shows while harness.json is being written.
fix: Append to both descriptions at plugins/arc-straps/config/arc-straps.schema.json:27-28 a clause such as ' Set apart from arc_meta.atbx / arc_meta.tool_dir; this section never reads arc_meta.'
Also add an arc_help_pages object to the README harness.json example (plugins/arc-straps/README.md:95-101) that repeats the arc_meta values, so the example shows both sections set together.

minor.name: help_page_unlinked ignores a page href that carries a #fragment, ?query or percent-encoding
minor.summary:
_links_page (lines 117-120) compares the href tail byte for byte with page_href's tail. _link_problem (line 86) strips '#'/'?' and unquotes the tail before checking it. So an href like <prefix>tool_metadata/tool_help/Tool.html#syntax, or one that percent-encodes a space in the page path, passes check_links but makes check_help_page report help_page_unlinked. The Judgment row (SKILL.md line 136) then tells the agent to add a second, redundant link.

Also (overall): _link_problem percent-decodes the tail (unquote, line 86) while _links_page compares the raw tail against page_href (line 120), and page_href (arc_help_pages_config.py:44) appends the repo path unencoded after an as_uri() prefix that is encoded. With a help_dir or page name holding a space, an href written as .../tool%20help/demo.html is clean for check_links but help_page_unlinked for check_help_page, and the href page_href prints carries a raw space.

Also (system_shape): `check_links` drops a `#...` or `?...` tail before resolving (`_link_problem` line 86), so `<prefix>tool_metadata/tool_help/demo.html#parameters` is a valid link. `_links_page` (lines 117-120) compares the whole tail after the prefix with the bare `page_href` tail, so the same href makes `check_help_page` report `help_page_unlinked`. A canonical XML that deep-links its page into one section passes one check and fails the other. SKILL.md:123 does not say an anchored link is excluded.
fix: Normalize the tail in _links_page the same way _link_problem does: split at the first # or ?, then unquote. Share one helper between the two and add a test for an href that ends in #section.

Compare decoded tails in _links_page (unquote both sides, dropping any #/? suffix as _link_problem does), and build page_href's tail with urllib.parse.quote so the printed href is a valid URI; add a test with a help_dir containing a space.

In `_links_page`, compare `re.split(r"[#?]", href[len(p.prefix):], maxsplit=1)[0]` with the page tail, sharing one helper with `_link_problem`, and add a case to `tests/arc/test_arc_help_pages_api.py` that links `page_href(PAGE) + "#parameters"` and expects `check_help_page` to be clean.

minor.name: A missing toolbox alias renders a broken syntax line
minor.summary:
_archive_facts returns alias '' when toolbox.content is absent, is not an object, or has no string alias. _syntax_section then renders 'arcpy..Tool(...)' without any warning, so the Python syntax section of the page is wrong and nothing reports it.

Also (overall): _archive_facts returns '' when toolbox.content has no string alias (source.py:156-157), and _syntax_section renders arcpy..Demo(...) from it (build.py:155). The page is built and reported current with a call no user can run.
fix: Raise HelpError in _archive_facts when toolbox.content is absent or the alias is empty or not a string, naming the archive.
In _syntax_section, render 'arcpy.<Tool>(...)' when the alias is empty, and document that.
Refuse in _archive_facts with HelpError(f"toolbox.content in {p.atbx.name} has no alias") so check_help_page reports it as a build refusal, and add a test using archive_members(alias='').

minor.name: _param_names accepts a tool.content without params despite its docstring
minor.summary: The docstring says the function refuses tool.content unless it holds a params object. The code reads content.get("params", {}), so a tool.content object with no params key passes as a dict and gives a page with an empty Parameters table instead of a refusal.
fix: If parameterless tools omit the key, keep the default and reword the docstring to say a missing params key reads as no parameters.
If a missing key is a defect, use content.get("params") so the isinstance check refuses it.

minor.name: API test module docstring describes check_links as reading only file: hrefs
minor.summary:
The module docstring (lines 5-7) says check_links reads every file: href and lists two codes; the code reads every href and also reports link_relative for scheme-less hrefs, which test_check_links_reports_relative_hrefs (line 142) pins. The docstring contradicts both the implementation and a test in the same file.

Also (system_shape): tests/arc/test_arc_help_pages_api.py:5-7 says `check_links` 'reads every `file:` href' and lists only `link_target_missing` and `link_outside_checkout`. The module under test also reports `link_relative` for scheme-less hrefs (api.py:73-81), and `test_check_links_reports_relative_hrefs` in the same file pins that behavior.
fix: Reword lines 5-7 to: check_links reads every href in a tool's canonical XML: anchors and non-file: schemes are skipped, a file: href under the checkout prefix must name a file in the current tree (link_target_missing), any other file: href is dead in production (link_outside_checkout), and a scheme-less href not rooted at / or \ is link_relative.
Extend the docstring: 'check_links reads every href: ... and an href with no scheme that is not rooted is `link_relative`; anchors and web links are skipped.'

minor.name: Skill contract docstring claims an ordering the test does not check
minor.summary: The module docstring (lines 5-6) says the contract pins that the procedure reads the tool's code before a fragment states anything, but test_the_procedure_names_its_sources_and_checks (lines 93-97) only asserts each phrase appears somewhere in the body; a SKILL.md that reads the entry module after writing the fragment still passes.
fix: Either drop 'before a fragment states anything' from the docstring and say the procedure names its sources and checks, or add an assertion that the first index of 'entry module' precedes the first mention of writing the fragment in the body.
